extra.message: In the vulnerable get_db_connection(), user-controlled post_id is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to conn.execute('SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = ' + post_id) instead of using a parameterized query, allowing SQL injection.

Multiple SQL injection patterns: user input (username) is concatenated/formatted into SQL query strings passed to cursor.execute() via '+', str.format, '%' and f-string interpolation. Each allows SQL injection because user input is placed directly into the query text instead of being passed as a bound parameter.

The username value (decrypted from the user-controlled session_id cookie at line 26) is written directly into the HTTP response with bytes("Hello %s" % username) without any HTML encoding, enabling cross-site scripting. Additionally the cookie is decrypted with AES-CBC and no message authentication (no HMAC), so a padding-oracle attack lets an attacker forge a cookie decrypting to an arbitrary username, making the XSS attacker-controllable.

extra.message: The payment signature is computed as hashlib.sha256(secret + payment_information), a secret-prefix MAC. This construction is vulnerable to hash length-extension attacks, allowing an attacker who captures a valid (message, signature) pair to forge valid signatures for an extended message (e.g., append/override payment parameters such as amount) without knowing the secret. HMAC should be used instead.

extra.message: The url parameter from request.args is fetched server-side via urllib.request.urlopen(url). The only validation, url.startswith('https://insecurewebapp.com'), is trivially bypassable (e.g., 'https://insecurewebapp.com@127.0.0.1/' uses the prefix as userinfo, or 'https://insecurewebapp.com.evil.com/' as a subdomain), enabling Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services or arbitrary hosts.

context.check_hostname = False disables TLS hostname verification on the SSL context. A man-in-the-middle attacker can present any valid certificate (issued for an unrelated, trusted domain) and impersonate the intended host, defeating server authentication.

User-controlled cookie data (cookies.get('username').value) is deserialized with pickle.loads (shown at line 15; the active code at line 14 delegates to Username.pickle() for this same cookie). pickle.loads on untrusted input enables arbitrary code execution, and no signature or integrity check is performed on the cookie before deserialization.

User-controlled self.path (the request URL path) is appended directly to the filesystem path (path += self.path at line 14) and then opened with open(path).read() at line 22. The only validation is a weak regex, re.match(r'/\.\.\/\.\.\/', self.path), which only blocks '/../../' anchored at the start of the string and is bypassable via URL-encoding (e.g. %2e%2e%2f), backslash variants, or placing the traversal sequence elsewhere, enabling path traversal and arbitrary file read.
